sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Distribution of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (applies to France)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF); Articles L.561-45 to L.561-49 CMF (mandatory beneficial-owner register); Décret n° 2016-1632 of 29 November 2016 and Arrêté of 23 June 2021 on the content and procedure of the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE); Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended and Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLA), transposed/implemented in French law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and certified copy of the valid passport (identity pages and signature) of each ultimate beneficial owner, director, and authorized company representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the jurisdiction of residence of the individual UBO/representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing State is a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization by the competent French Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, registration excerpt, or equivalent corporate good-standing certificate of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the country of registration of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (as appropriate for origin state), followed by approved French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence of each corporate shareholder and of each UBO whose fiscal status is relevant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national tax authority in the jurisdiction of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with notarized translation into French if required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank KYC/reference letter evidencing the AML profile of the shareholders and source of funds / source of wealth
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution maintaining the account of the shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of authorized bank officers; overseas bank letters may require apostille depending on the origin State; notarized translation into French

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, legal representatives, and shareholders against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, France's national freezing list (Fichier des sanctions financières, FSF), and, where relevant to USD transactions, the OFAC SDN list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified using the statutory definition in Article R.561-18 CMF. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, high-risk third countries, and non-face-to-face relationships. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years as set out in Articles L.561-34 and L.561-34-2 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for electronic filings; Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) for company and RCS lookup; INPI (data.inpi.fr) for trademark and company-availability verification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be in French or a foreign language using Latin characters. If a proposed name uses a non-Latin script (e.g. Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek), a transliteration in Latin characters must be filed. The name must include the suffix 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' and must not infringe prior trademarks, trade names or company names. The name must not be misleading or contrary to public order; compliance with Articles R.123-52 et seq. of the French Code de commerce is assessed at the time of registration by the RCS/Greffe.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation issued by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce is valid for 30 days and cannot be extended; after expiry, a fresh request is required. If the RCS/Greffe rejects the requested name, the applicant may submit a cure request (régularisation) through the Guichet unique within one month, amending the articles of association and/or proposing a new name. If the refusal persists, the applicant may file a recours gracieux with the Greffier and a recours hiérarchique with the local Procureur de la République, or initiate summary judicial proceedings (référé) before the président du Tribunal de Commerce to compel registration. Any judicial appeal must be filed within one month of notification of the refusal; legal counsel should monitor all timelines because the 30-day reservation window will not be suspended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial domiciliation agent is permitted for the corporate registered office under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Code de commerce. However, this is insufficient for the licensed pharmaceutical API wholesale business. The Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM) requires a dedicated physical establishment (storage, handling and administrative office) that complies with Good Distribution Practice (GDP) and is available for inspection. A pure virtual registered office will trigger rejection of company registration and any subsequent pharmaceutical wholesale licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – approximately 80% quantified probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by ANSM and/or DGCCRF within the first 12 months of obtaining the initial pharmaceutical API wholesale registration, due to the high-risk nature, the GDP requirements, and France's strengthened post-market supervision regime upheld by Articles L.5124-3 et seq. of the French Public Health Code.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French legal counsel for SAS lex societatis, due diligence and drafting of articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate / fixed professional fee, not a statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability searches in the RCS, INPI, Infogreffe and trademark databases
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI / Infogreffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry fees approximately EUR 8–20 per search; commercial supplier charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the legal notice (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorized in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per line / competitive gazette rate, normally EUR 150–300

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and/or consular legalization bundle for passport, corporate documents, tax residence and KYC evidence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public (foreign or French), competent consulate, and/or apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariffs and consular fees; translation/interpreter costs at market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official certification and translation into French of foreign public documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified expert translator (French court-appointed, expert près la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per page; statutory for certificated translation where required

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner (UBO/RBE) declaration preparation and submission through the Guichet unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-based legal support fee; not a statutory registry fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and international sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors and corporate shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/KYC data screening technology provider (e.g. Dow Jones / World-Check equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial subscription license per entity, not statutory

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary declaration of the API wholesale distribution activity with ANSM (établissement pharmaceutique and substances actives registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative levy/charge for the preliminary declaration and initial inspection file (estimate, subject to ANSM tariff schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation bank account opening and bank KYC compliance support for the SAS project
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French licensed bank / financial institution according to the project bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for account opening and KYC processing; no statutory standard fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Reservation of the corporate name (réservation de nom) at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (optional procedure)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce compétent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 et seq., L.224-1 et seq., L.227-1 to L.227-30; implementing rules R.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); French Civil Code rules on juridical persons.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (articles of association), declaration of constitution in the RCS M0 formalities, certificat de parution in a legal gazette, attestation of blocked funds, and declaration of the beneficial owner.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an SAS, the law imposes no minimum capital; the capital is fixed in the articles. If cash is subscribed, the full subscribed amount (or the shareholder-defined instalments expressly accepted in the articles) must be deposited into a French bank blocked account or with Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations before filing. The blocked sum is released to the President immediately after issuance of the Kbis. Non-cash contributions are valued by a commissaire aux apports unless exempted, and are paid in full upon contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: By unanimous shareholder consent, resolved: (1) the share capital of EUR [•] in the Articles is subscribed and paid up under Article L.227-1, Code de commerce; (2) the registered office is set at [French address], within the competent Greffe's jurisdiction; (3) [President] is appointed President with full powers of ordinary and extraordinary representation; (4) the President is authorized to publish the legal notice, complete the Guichet Unique filing and obtain the Kbis; and (5) the President shall apply without delay for the ANSM pharmaceutical establishment authorization required for active pharmaceutical ingredient wholesale distribution. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription, Blocked Account, and Bank Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each founding shareholder subscribes to the draft share capital; the President or a designated founder opens a blocked cash deposit account at a French bank or CDC in the company's name. Fund transfer must be documented; the bank issues an attestation de blocage de fonds. No notarization is required at this stage unless the shareholders require it or an in-kind contribution must be valued.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of each shareholder and beneficial owner
Power of attorney if an agent subscribes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account, select another eligible bank or use CDC. If the attestation is returned with discrepancies, request a corrected attestation before filing with the Guichet Unique; no formal adverse action exists at this stage because blocking is internal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Signature of Statuts and Appointment of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders; notaire mandatory only for certain in-kind contributions or real property contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the articles with the company name, purpose (wholesale distribution and import/export of active pharmaceutical ingredients), duration, registered office, capital, share classes, governance structure and rights. All shareholders sign or electronically countersign the articles. The President is appointed either in the articles or by a separate written decision and accepts office in writing. The registered office and the scope of the President's powers are formally recorded.
required_dossiers: President's acceptance letter / act of appointment
Registered office proof (lease, free occupancy agreement, or ownership document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or notaire notes an irregularity in signature clauses, amend and restate the articles and re-execute; if foreign shareholders are involved, provide certified French translation before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obligatory Legal Announcement in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal gazette in the department of the registered office / media approved by the prefecture
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft an avis de constitution containing the required statutory particulars: SAS corporate form, company name, capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, President's identity and RCS town. Submit the notice to an approved legal gazette and pay the publication fee. Obtain the certificat de parution, which must be included in the RCS filing. Publish the notice only after final execution of the statuts.
required_dossiers: Registered office address justification if required by the gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal gazette rejects the notice because statutory elements are omitted, correct and resubmit. The JAL certificate remains valid only if issued within the statutory period before filing; if expired, republish and obtain a fresh certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Dossier Submission to the Guichet Unique and RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (INPI) and the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and complete the full incorporation formalities for an SAS. Attach the signed statuts, JAL certificate, bank attestation, powers, identity documents, non-condemnation declaration and beneficial owner declaration. The Guichet Unique performs formal compliance control, forwards the dossier to the RCS registry, and, after payment of duties and registration fees, the Greffe registers the company and issues SIREN/SIRET and the Kbis extract. The applicant receives a recepisse with a file number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries or rejects the dossier for incompleteness, file the requested rectificative act within 15 days of notification. If the refusal is substantive, contest through the presiding judge of the Tribunal de Commerce or the Tribunal Judiciaire under Article R.123-102 of the Commercial Code, then refile the corrected dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Kbis, SIRET/APE Code, and Post-Registration Social and Tax Coordination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE, URSSAF, DGFiP
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Greffe issues the Kbis extract. INSEE assigns the SIREN and SIRET numbers and the APE/NAF code appropriate to wholesale pharmaceutical distribution. DGFiP and URSSAF receive the registration via the Guichet Unique. The President opens the operational corporate bank account, obtains RIB details, and initiates any employer registrations if hiring will begin. The company also establishes its statutory corporate records and governance calendar before commencing regulated activities.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or free occupation attestation
DGFiP tax and VAT identification output
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIREN/APE is incorrect in relation to the declared activity, apply for rectification at INSEE through the Greffe. If fiscal or social registrations are not received, contact the local SIE and URSSAF with the Kbis and statuts; late registration can be regularized, subject to any applicable surcharges if filing deadlines were missed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: ANSM (Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé) for pharmaceutical establishment licensing; DREETS for occupational safety; DREAL for ICPE/environmental permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement pharmaceutique / autorisation de distribution en gros et d'importation de matières premières à usage pharmaceutique (Articles L.5124-3, L.5124-13 and L.5124-18 of the French Public Health Code), together with conformity with the Bonnes Pratiques de Distribution (BPD).

environmental_impact_assessment.agency_name: DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement) and the préfecture-deposited environmental authorization procedure under Code de l'environnement, Livre V.
environmental_impact_assessment.classification_tier: Non-manufacturing wholesale distribution of APIs in France is generally not subject to a full environmental impact assessment unless it involves large warehouse volumes, storage of classified dangerous substances, or a sensitive geographic location. The typical classification is ICPE 'Déclaration' under sections 1510/1436 for low-hazard chemical storage, or 'Enregistrement' when threshold limits require an impact assessment; a full EIA applies only to the top-tier 'Autorisation' category.
environmental_impact_assessment.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Article R.512-1 et seq. and ICPE operating rules: no untreated release of pharmaceutical solids or chemicals to sewer; wastewater must meet local municipal discharge limits (pH 5.5–9.5, COD ≤ 300 mg/l, BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/l, suspended solids ≤ 100 mg/l, phosphorus ≤ 10 mg/l, temperature ≤ 30°C); storage and handling must respect REACH/CLP labelling, sealed container systems and VOC abatement where applicable; hazardous pharmaceutical waste must be moved only by licensed carriers and recorded in the register of waste/BSD.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operations, obtain the fire safety attestation from the local sécurité civile/SDIS or the competent commission de sécurité where the premises qualify as ERP, a structural load survey/attestation certifying the load capacity of any storage areas, an electrical installation verification certificate, and an occupational health and safety clearance from DREETS under the French Labour Code. The site must be registered with the relevant authorities and a workplace health and safety file established before storage or distribution of APIs begins.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères for non-established businesses. Official portals: https://www.impots.gouv.fr and https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Customs and EORI matters are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through https://www.douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated through the one-stop business formalities portal operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The registration produces a SIREN identifier for the legal entity, a SIRET identifier for each establishment, and a Kbis extract. The DGFiP then assigns or confirms the French VAT identification number, generally formatted as FR followed by two check digits and the nine-digit SIREN. The company must register with the competent SIE, provide its articles of association, Kbis, registered-office evidence, beneficial-owner information, business activity description, bank details, expected turnover, intra-Community transaction profile, and evidence supporting the pharmaceutical wholesale activity. A foreign entity carrying on taxable transactions in France must apply to the competent French tax office or the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères for a French VAT number. An entity established in the European Union generally may register directly without appointing a French fiscal representative. A non-EU entity generally must appoint an accredited French fiscal representative unless an applicable legal or administrative exception applies. Importers and customs representatives should obtain an EORI number from the DGDDI before importing or exporting APIs. VAT registration may be required even where the domestic turnover franchise threshold is not exceeded, including for imports, intra-Community acquisitions, and transactions for which the business elects or is required to charge French VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). It may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime if statutory conditions are satisfied, including generally that the company is newly formed, unlisted, carries on an eligible commercial, industrial, artisanal, agricultural, or professional activity, remains below the applicable employee and turnover or balance-sheet limits, and obtains the required shareholder approval. The election is limited in duration and cannot normally be renewed after its statutory period. An SAS does not have a general U.S.-style check-the-box election. France has no general elective hybrid-mismatch classification regime; anti-hybrid rules under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance framework may deny deductions or impose inclusion consequences where statutory conditions are met. VAT grouping, tax consolidation, and other group regimes are separate elections subject to their own eligibility requirements and do not change the SAS's basic legal-entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), integrated with the European Union VAT system. Customs duties and import VAT apply separately to imports from outside the European Union.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For businesses eligible for the French domestic VAT franchise, the ordinary annual turnover threshold is generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and related activities, including wholesale distribution, with a higher tolerance threshold generally of EUR 93,500. The corresponding service thresholds are generally EUR 37,500 and EUR 41,250. Thresholds and sector-specific rules must be checked for the relevant tax year. These thresholds do not eliminate registration requirements arising from imports, intra-Community acquisitions, distance sales, reverse-charge obligations, voluntary taxation, or other taxable transactions. A French SAS conducting pharmaceutical API wholesale activity should normally obtain a VAT number at commencement where it imports, exports, or trades intra-Community, irrespective of domestic turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting rather than a current universal real-time clearance model. All French businesses must be capable of receiving compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Large and medium-sized businesses must issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises generally must issue them from 1 September 2027. Electronic invoices must use an approved structured or hybrid format and be transmitted through an approved private electronic invoicing platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, PDP), subject to the final operating rules. B2C and cross-border transaction data will generally be reported electronically under the e-reporting framework. France does not currently require a universal pre-clearance stamp or real-time government validation for every invoice. Businesses must retain invoices and supporting VAT records for the statutory retention period and ensure reconciliation between invoices, customs declarations, VAT returns, Intrastat declarations, and accounting records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT where the supplier is established or VAT-registered as required, the goods are actually dispatched or transported outside the EU, the supplier is identified as exporter or otherwise satisfies the applicable export conditions, and the export is supported by customs evidence showing exit from the EU. The export exemption is not available merely because an invoice states that the transaction is an export. For intra-Community supplies to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State, the separate intra-Community supply exemption applies only if the statutory conditions are met, including valid customer VAT identification, transport to another Member State, and required reporting. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France are generally outside the scope of French VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule rather than technically zero-rated; the supplier must retain evidence of the customer's business status and establishment. Services connected with goods, transport, customs, and regulated pharmaceutical activities require transaction-specific place-of-supply analysis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration containing the consignor, consignee, commodity classification, customs value, origin, procedure, and movement reference number
MRN and electronic exit confirmation or equivalent customs evidence, including the Export Accompanying Document and IE-599 or successor exit message where applicable
Commercial invoice identifying the goods, quantities, prices, Incoterms, VAT treatment, exporter, and consignee
Packing list and transport document, such as bill of lading, air waybill, rail consignment note, or road consignment note
Proof of transport and delivery outside the European Union, including carrier or freight-forwarder evidence
Import customs evidence or destination-country customs records where necessary to corroborate exit and delivery
Valid EORI information and, where applicable, customs power of attorney and export authorization records
For regulated pharmaceutical APIs, applicable product, export, quality, controlled-substance, and customs licensing records
Banking and payment records supporting the commercial transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a standard French VAT export document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange control requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. The exporter must nevertheless retain reliable commercial, customs, transport, payment, and accounting evidence and comply with applicable anti-money-laundering, sanctions, customs, and pharmaceutical controls. If export exemption is incorrectly claimed, the DGFiP may assess the unpaid VAT retrospectively, together with late-payment interest and tax penalties. Deliberate or materially negligent inaccuracies may attract penalties commonly ranging from 40% for deliberate failure to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, subject to the applicable facts and statutory limits. A VAT credit or refund obtained without entitlement may be clawed back with interest and penalties. False customs declarations may trigger customs duties, import VAT, customs fines, seizure, and other sanctions. Serious intentional tax fraud may additionally result in criminal prosecution, including imprisonment and substantial fines; aggravated tax-fraud cases may carry significantly higher penalties. Export documentation must therefore be complete, internally consistent, and capable of being matched to the customs exit record, invoice, logistics chain, VAT return, and accounting ledger.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as national competent authority for foreign-exchange data collection and balance-of-payments reporting under Articles L141-6 and R141-7 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, acting within the euro-area framework of the European Central Bank; the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) administers exchange-control and foreign-investment screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible across current and capital account operations. France imposes no exchange controls on trade or financial flows, subject to the EU free movement of capital (Article 63 TFEU) and the OECD Code of Liberalisation. Profit remittance to foreign parents is unrestricted, but dividends to non-EU shareholders incur a 25% withholding tax (12.8% plus social levies), reduced under applicable tax treaties; qualifying EU parents benefit from the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) at 0% withholding. Capital inflows require no prior authorization. Any cross-border transfer exceeding EUR 7,500 must be reported to the Banque de France via the intermediary bank for balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in France. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained, converted, or used for payments at the SAS's discretion. The sole statutory obligation is the Banque de France declaration regime (Articles R152-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code): each transfer between France and a non-resident exceeding EUR 7,500 must be declared through the banking intermediary. For operational efficiency, the entity should invoice in EUR or USD and convert via treasury hedging rails rather than rely on forced conversion timelines.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (with dedicated capital escrow sub-ledger)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury function. French or EEA-authorised e-money institutions and payment institutions cannot issue documentary letters of credit or provide the credit facilities required for pharmaceutical API trade flows, and French tier-1 banks treat EMI accounts as non-qualifying for capital and creditor-protection purposes. Non-EU digital EMIs (notably post-Brexit UK e-money firms) may not operate in France without an EEA passport or local agency; even where passporting exists, the high-risk pharma classification confines EMIs to ancillary collections and payables automation. All principal liquidity and trade-finance rails must remain with tier-1 credit institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the non-resident directors/UBOs under this high-risk profile. French AML law (Articles L561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code and ACPR guidance) requires an in-person 'entretien de conformité' at the bank or with its certified international relation officers; remote onboarding is effectively unavailable for a non-resident-owned pharma API wholesale SAS. The interviewed party must present a valid passport and, for non-EU individuals, a certified 10-year criminal record extract and notarized corporate documents; a locally domiciled legal representative may attend, but the beneficial owner interview is typically waived only where the home bank provides a 'Relations Internationales' guarantee to the French institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material beneficial ownership opacity with a non-EU UBO chain (China, India, UAE) holding 25% or more.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled corporate registry extracts with sworn French translation; updated UBO declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) filed at the RCS/INPI with receipt; passport copies certified by a notary or consulate; bank reference letters via SWIFT confirmation from the UBO's existing banker; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement; shareholders' register and share transfer history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale classification (ISIC 4649 / NACE 46.46) with counterfeit and gray-market exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid ANSM wholesale distribution authorization or registered pharmacist attestation; EU Good Distribution Practices (GDP) certificate and latest inspection report; ISO 9001 and applicable GMP certifications; batch-level Certificates of Analysis for every traded API; vendor and customer due-diligence file restricted to authorized downstream wholesalers; pharmacovigilance and product-liability statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment corridors (China, India, Brazil, Turkey) with advance-payment patterns to foreign API manufacturers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade documentation: signed purchase/sales contracts, pro-forma and commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, certificates of origin, independent third-party laboratory reports, customs declarations (Export/SAL summaries), and banker's opinions from correspondent banks; adherence to Wolfsberg Trade Finance Principles and FATF recommendations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, dual-use and precursor chemical screening concerns on select APIs and raw materials.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions and export-control compliance policy; live screening against EU (Regulation 269/2014), OFAC, UN, and UK HMT lists; product-level classification ruling confirming non-dual-use status under Regulation (EU) 2021/821; end-user certificates and end-use declaration where any precursor content is flagged; traceable country-of-origin documentation to support customs valuation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax residence and transfer-pricing credibility gaps in a BEPS-sensitive structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French corporate tax residence certificate issued by the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques; attestation de régularité fiscale confirming no unpaid taxes; BEPS Action 13 transfer-pricing documentation for the pharmaceutical wholesale margin (typically 5-8% net under a Transactional Net Margin Method); audited financial statements; CRS and DAC6 disclosure confirmations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103/MT202 destined for the SAS's French tier-1 bank account, referencing the capital-increase resolution and Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code S008 (acquisition de participation). Funds must arrive in EUR in the name of FR_SAS and be credited to a dedicated capital escrow account; the bank issues an attestation de libération des fonds enabling the notary or counsel to file amended articles at the RCS. The originator BIC and legal name must appear to comply with Regulation (EU) 2015/847; the bank files the mandatory declaration for any transfer exceeding EUR 7,500, and the capital must be unencumbered and fully clear before disbursement to trade creditors.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 for open-account and cash-advance supplier payments (standard terms 30% cash in advance, 70% against shipping documents) with BiP import purpose codes; irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued by the French bank via SWIFT MT700 for first trades with Chinese and Indian API makers, settled via MT400/MT202 upon compliant presentation; standby LC (MT760) for contractual performance; SEPA Credit Transfer for EU suppliers in EUR; all outgoing transfers pass through sanctions, KYC, and counterparty screening and require explicit balance-of-payments purpose codes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD plain-vanilla FX forward (option ferme de change) with tenors up to 18 months under a bank collateral or margin-line arrangement.
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on CNY/USD, INR/USD and BRL/USD for corridor settlements with non-convertible currencies, cash-settled in EUR.
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD CCS) to convert USD trade receivables into EUR liquidity and hedge interest-rate mismatches.
European-style purchased FX options on EUR/USD and CNY/USD with premium payment under EMIR-compliant terms.
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) with a tier-1 banking counterpart under ISDA 2002 architecture and the EMIR non-financial-counterparty hedging exemption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts, allocation of profit, and filing of shareholder resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS shareholders; corporate records maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after the financial year-end; resolutions must be recorded in the decision minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court injunction and daily penalty payment; failure to prepare or approve accounts may trigger director liability and statutory sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry and National Register of Enterprises (RNE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a court injunction, daily penalty payment, and criminal fines generally up to EUR 1,500, increased for repeat offences; no automatic fixed strike-off deadline applies solely for late accounts filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronically by the second working day after 1 May for a calendar-year company, subject to the applicable annual tax filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, interest for late payment, and possible increased penalties for concealment or repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and related VAT reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual CA12 return within the applicable filing period for the simplified VAT regime; monthly or quarterly VAT returns apply under the normal regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, and additional penalties depending on the conduct and tax impact

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information review and filing of amendments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry and National Register of Enterprises (RNE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No general annual confirmation filing; review annually and file changes generally within 30 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may result in injunctive measures, criminal fines, and restrictions affecting registry compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant assessment date: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional requirements may apply to certain groups, controlled entities, or regulated activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Plan (Plan comptable général). IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts or where legally elected; IFRS is not generally mandatory for standalone SAS accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual standalone UBO confirmation. The company should perform an annual internal verification of ownership and control data and file an amendment with the competent registry promptly after any change, generally within 30 days. Shareholding transfers must also be reflected in the shareholder accounts and share transfer register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or shareholder accounts
Minute book of shareholder and corporate decisions
Beneficial ownership documentation and filed declarations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 600-2,400 per year, approximately USD 650-2,600, depending on address, mail handling, and corporate services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,000-12,000 per year, approximately USD 3,300-13,100, depending on transaction volume, inventory, pharmaceutical compliance controls, group reporting, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard French corporate income tax rate; 15% reduced rate applies to the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 10 million, and a 3.3% social surcharge applies on additional CIT payable by groups with turnover above EUR 7.63 million and tax liability exceeding EUR 763,000).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Available incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% on eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that cap; Patent Box reduced rate of 10% on qualifying industrial property income; 95% participation exemption on qualifying subsidiary dividends; reduced IS rate for small and medium enterprises; five-year amortization or immediate deduction for certain software and pharmaceutical process patents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa No. 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultats) forming the annual liasse fiscale with schedules 2050 through 2059, filed electronically through the EFI/EDI portal of the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (impots.gouv.fr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly CIT instalments are payable in March, June, September, and December during the current fiscal year, with the final balance due with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the 2065-SD return and final payment must be filed by 3 May of the following calendar year; for any other fiscal-year close, the return is due within 3 months of the year-end, unless an extension is obtained under the EFI online-filing procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, legal form (SAS), SIREN/SIRET, APE/NAF code, registered office address, shareholders, and group membership information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French SAS wholly or partly owned by non-residents, use the French registered office as the filing address; do not claim the foreign shareholders' residence as the place of tax filing, and disclose ultimate beneficial owners if requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Case XG — Résultat fiscal (Taxable Income or Loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for tax additions and deductions, including correction of expenses not actually incurred and arm's-length adjustments on intra-group transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an API bulk wholesale SAS, ensure intercompany purchases from affiliated foreign suppliers are priced at arm's length; enter the adjusted taxable result and attach the transfer-pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses used to reduce current-year taxable income, subject to the statutory annual deduction cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses recorded within the French tax entity may be offset; losses of the non-resident shareholder or affiliated foreign API manufacturer cannot be utilised inside the French SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre 'Plus-values et moins-values' (Capital Gains and Losses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Short-term and long-term capital gains and losses, including disposals of intangible pharmaceutical assets, patents, and industrial property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border IP licensing, state the gross royalty and document the withholding tax relief or treaty claim on the applicable annex schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of CIR claimed against corporate income tax, with supporting R&D expenditure schedules and technical forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If R&D is performed outside France by a foreign affiliate, the credit is generally unavailable; for contract research performed in France, retain technical monitoring documents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge on the tax due if no formal notice was issued, rising to 40% after formal notice and 80% for bad faith or abuse of law; unpaid CIT also attracts a 5% late-payment penalty plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; criminal penalties may apply for deliberate failure to file.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic dividend withholding tax under Article 119 bis of the French General Tax Code (CGI) for dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the shareholder holds at least 10% of the capital for 2 years; treaty rates may reduce the rate to 10%, 5%, or 0%, depending on the residence treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA or EU directive rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of its country of residence; the French paying company may apply the reduced rate at source only if the shareholder provides a signed statement of actual ownership and holding-period compliance under Article 119 ter CGI. Where relief was not applied at source, the recipient must file a refund claim before 31 December of the second year following the receipt of the distributed dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding tax on patent, trademark, process, and know-how royalties paid by a French debtor to non-residents is 25%, but many French tax treaties reduce royalties to 0% or 5% (subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership proof); bank and trade interest paid to non-resident corporate lenders is generally exempt from French source withholding tax at the domestic level and is taxed under DTA at 0%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the specific treaty and lender type.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million in annual turnover or total assets (or control by an entity satisfying this threshold) triggers the mandatory French Master File, Local File, annual transfer-pricing declaration (Form 2257-SD), and notification of transfer-pricing documentation (Form 2258-SD); upon a written tax-administration request, the documentation must be supplied within 30 days.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute of the UAE type; however, economic substance is decisive under Article 57 CGI transfer-pricing recharacterisation, Article 209 B deemed abandonment of profit, the abuse-of-law doctrine under Articles L64/L64A of the Book of Tax Procedures, and the OECD Principal Purpose Test in DTAs. A French API wholesale SAS must maintain real premises, qualified personnel, inventory storage, logistical decision-making, and supporting contracts to preserve DTA and EU directive benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — Fraudulent Filing / Concealment of Profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to file the annual 2065-SD return, under-reporting of API turnover, creation of false invoices, or routing sales through a shell supplier in a low-tax territory while the French SAS retains the economic functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative surcharge up to 80% of the tax under-assessed (40% in cases of deliberate misstatement, 10% for simple late filing), plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%; criminal conviction for tax fraud can lead to imprisonment up to 5 years and criminal fines determined under Article 1741 CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be declared jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt and penalties under Article 1743 CGI; travel bans, management disqualification, freezing of personal assets, and imprisonment are possible upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law (Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A French SAS used solely as an invoicing pass-through for pharmaceutical API transactions, with no office, inventory, employees, or management in France, and with the entire commercial substance located abroad, resulting in the artificial avoidance of French corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax administration may disregard the arrangement as an abuse of law, re-attribute income to the true economic operator, impose the 80% abuse-of-law penalty on the reassessed tax, and deny treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who knowingly signed the sham transactions may be subject to the personal recovery of taxes and penalties as well as criminal prosecution for participating in the fraudulent scheme; civil courts may pierce the veil and order restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Intra-Group Margin Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or supply the Master File/Local File and Form 2257-SD despite crossing the EUR 400 million threshold; absent comparability analysis; use of unexplainable profit mark-ups on APIs purchased from related foreign suppliers; or settlement of intercompany debt against unrecorded receivables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The burden of proof shifts to the taxpayer; the tax administration may reconstruct the arm's-length margin and re-assess CIT; failure to respond to the documentation request within 30 days exposes the company to an automatic fine under Article 1740 A of the CGI and, in aggravated cases, the 40% or 80% surcharge with late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false transfer-pricing certificates or concealing documentation risk management disqualification and joint civil liability; egregious cases are prosecuted together with tax fraud, which may result in travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Abusive Financial Routing (AML/CFT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of high-risk third-party companies in the pharmaceutical API supply chain to layer payments through serial Swift LC or bank-wire transfers without verifying beneficial owners; accepting funds under false supply contracts; failing to maintain effective AML due diligence and transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the French Monetary and Financial Code may expose the company to fines up to EUR 1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years for named officers; the competent authority may order freezing of bank accounts, confiscation of the fraudulent proceeds, and liquidation proceedings; customs penalties can be added for false import declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed to criminal imprisonment, personal fines, travel bans, and civil damages; French courts may impose asset-freezing orders and enter judgments directly against personal holdings where the corporate structure is used as a vehicle for money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed or Non-Compliant Pharmaceutical Wholesale Operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wholesaling active pharmaceutical ingredients without the required authorisation under the French Public Health Code, operating without a responsible pharmacist, relabelling or re-importing APIs outside EU/EEA GMP conditions, or placing falsified API batches into the French market.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ANSM may suspend or withdraw the wholesale authorisation, order immediate closure of the storage site, and impose administrative fines; criminal penalties include imprisonment and fines for endangering public health; tax deductions relating to prohibited activities are disallowed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an unlawful pharmaceutical wholesale operation may be barred from commercial activity, held personally liable for public-health damage, and subject to criminal penalties including imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced where distribution was carried on without the statutory licence.
